semantics.rule: Every row retains seven independent states. Profile cells describe source applicability, not tested Cartesian-product support. No global PASS.
semantics.acceptance_rule: Exact historical accepted candidate only; current dependency closure is not inferred from file or version equality.
semantics.scope: Selected backend CLI, core relationships, explicit typed/composition/runtime/application and minted-project profiles. Historical/research portfolio disposition belongs to DSR-002/041.
semantics.not_applicable: Unsupported axis combination, not a passing product cell; all real selected promises still require DSR-018/029 tests.

types.label: Entity
types.meaning: Identity-bearing domain object; no automatic persistence.

types.label: Value Object
types.meaning: Value semantics and invariant references; shared typed-record representation does not collapse identity distinctions.

types.label: Enum
types.meaning: Closed variants; typed sum has payloads.

types.label: Operation
types.meaning: Declared reads/writes/effects; generated code and host/provider runtime are separate.

types.label: Query
types.meaning: Typed row evaluator or typed read-only closure; untyped fallback differs by language.

types.label: Calculation
types.meaning: Pure arithmetic; current source graph still requires an outgoing calculates relationship.

types.label: Rule
types.meaning: Boolean assertion; typed semantics required for evaluation.

types.label: Policy
types.meaning: Selects target/strategy; does not execute it. Static Rules and typed inline predicates differ.

types.label: Workflow
types.meaning: Orchestration/recovery models and in-process recovery helpers; no general durable workflow executor.

types.label: Interface
types.meaning: Versioned boundary signatures and compatibility checks, not network transport.

types.label: Event
types.meaning: Versioned occurrence/payload identity, not event delivery.

types.label: Mapping
types.meaning: Field transformation with source/target roles; not implicit calculation dependency.

types.label: State Machine
types.meaning: Transition helpers exist; trigger/output relationship mismatch remains.

relationships.semantics: An entity or actor initiates an operation.
An operation causes an event on successful completion.
An operation writes or projects data into an entity owned by another feature.
An operation canonically owns bringing new identity-bearing instances of one same-feature entity type into existence on successful execution.
An event in one feature activates an operation in another feature.
A rule gates whether an operation may execute. The same canonical verb applies within one feature or across feature boundaries; placement carries the scope, not a second verb.
A calculation derives values used by an operation.
An event advances a state machine.
An interface makes an operation or query callable.
A workflow coordinates ordered operations within one feature or across declared feature boundaries.
A policy selects behavior for an operation or calculation.
A mapping transforms data between an entity and an interface or between boundary shapes.
An entity embeds a value object as part of its field structure.
An operation or query depends on entity data by reading it, without making the target an owner or implying that the whole source behavior is read-only.
An entity is the subject/source of a domain event.
An entity has lifecycle, custody, or write-responsibility ownership over another entity.
An entity is a member of, classified by, or assigned to another entity. This is distinct from owns^-1.
A page renders components.
A layout wraps pages.
A component includes child components.
A component consumes a hook for state or data.
A form validates input and delegates to an action.
An adapter shapes data into a view model.
A guard controls access to a page.
A component displays a view model.
A UI binding fetches from a backend query.
A UI binding invokes a backend operation.
A UI state indicator mirrors a backend state machine.
A view model is derived from entity fields.
A form schema aligns with an interface contract.
A client-side guard mirrors a backend access rule.

gaps.title: Dispatcher-only application commands
gaps.meaning: Two current native commands are absent from capability/help metadata.

gaps.title: Untyped Query and Rule are not complete evaluators
gaps.meaning: Untyped Query copies state in TypeScript/Python and panics in Rust; untyped Rule throws/panics.

gaps.title: State Machine trigger/output confusion
gaps.meaning: Incoming transitions Event is checked against effect_event_ref; trigger and output roles are conflated.

gaps.title: Workflow target identity is not occurrence identity
gaps.meaning: Relationship checks use unique bare Operation IDs; general execution and qualified occurrence semantics are not implied.

gaps.title: Multiplicity and ownership axes need reconciliation
gaps.meaning: Current validator applies verb-level multiplicity and inverse-collapse checks; this does not implement all BMC ownership/membership dimensions.

gaps.title: Composition certificate and checked assurance differ
gaps.meaning: Project certificates include compositions; checked interchange rejects them. Neither proves general runtime execution.

gaps.title: Default test denominator omits candidate suites
gaps.meaning: outbound-composition, request-custody, service-security and stream-lifecycle test files exist but are absent from test:proof/test:parallel.

gaps.title: Accepted archive is not the current source tree
gaps.meaning: Exact accepted successor identity is preserved separately from changed source and the output-layout candidate.

gaps.title: Policy profiles use different condition models
gaps.meaning: Static Policy reuses declared Rules; typed-policy uses inline predicates. Do not silently call these identical.

gaps.title: Nested types and storage are distinct contracts
